summary: The RLS policy uses `using (true)`, so any authenticated user can read every invoice in public.invoices. Restrict it to the owner, for example `auth.uid() = user_id`.
SQL injection: the `q` and `sort` parameters are interpolated directly into a `$queryRawUnsafe` string. Use parameterized `$queryRaw` for the term and an allowlist for the sort column.

Accessibility: the email input has no associated label and relies only on placeholder text, so it lacks a reliable accessible name. Add a visible <label> (or aria-label) and use type="email" with autocomplete="email".

The PaymentIntent amount and currency come straight from the client request body, so a user can pay any price they choose. Compute the amount server-side from trusted product or cart data, and require authentication and validation.
The search term is parameterized with LIKE wildcards escaped, and sort is restricted to an allowlist of Prisma.sql fragments. No issues found.
A Supabase service_role JWT is hardcoded in frontend code. It bypasses RLS and gives anyone full database access. Revoke and rotate it now, and use the anon/publishable key on the client.

Open finding AG-001 (high, confirmed by a failing runtime test at the head commit): any signed-in user can read another user's invoice. Green unit tests do not override it, so the release is NO-GO until it is fixed and re-verified.

Reliability: saveNote retries immediately with no backoff and ignores network exceptions. After three failures it returns silently, so the user's note is lost without any error. The POST also has no Content-Type header and no idempotency key, so retries can create duplicate notes.

readInvoices uses an admin (privileged) database client and returns every invoice with no authentication or user scoping. Any caller of this tool can read all customers' invoices. Scope the query to the authenticated user and use a least-privilege client.
This is a Supabase publishable key, which is meant to be exposed to clients. No issue, provided RLS is enforced on the data.
The route requires an authenticated user, checks invoice ownership, and returns 404 for both missing and unowned invoices. No issues found.
IDOR / missing authentication: the route returns any invoice by ID with no authentication or ownership check. Require a user and verify invoice.userId matches, returning 404 otherwise.
Documentation-only change that fixes a typo in the README. No security, privacy, reliability, or accessibility impact.

Race condition (TOCTOU): the redeemed check and the update are separate, non-atomic operations, so concurrent requests can redeem the same coupon more than once. Use a conditional update (where code and redeemed=false) or a transaction, and check the affected row count.

Premium is unlocked just by rendering the success page, with no server-side check that payment succeeded. Anyone can reach the page and get premium for free. Grant entitlements only from a verified payment webhook or a server-side payment status check.
The RLS policy limits authenticated users to selecting their own invoices via auth.uid() = user_id. No issues found.

The audit data contradicts the GO summary: an open, confirmed critical finding (service-role credential in client code) and a failed critical mandatory check (secrets). The finding's commit also does not match the head commit. Record NO-GO until the key is rotated, removed, and re-verified.

Static review shows the route enforces authentication and an ownership check (returning 404 for other users' invoices). With no database, test run, or staging environment, the ownership check could not be executed, so it is recorded as NOT TESTED rather than PASS.
